name: runtime_owner_285
algorithm: Scans an 8-byte-entry, id==-1-terminated table at 0x0809d9f0 ({s16 id; s16 value:15; u16 alt_source:1; s16 condition; s16 result}). For each entry: if alt_source is set, require entry.id == Data_02000240[224] (the established 'scene/progress id' cell); otherwise require entry.id == Data_02000240[230]. Then require entry.value == -1 (wildcard) or entry.value == Data_02000240[225] (the established scene sub-state cell). Then require entry.condition == -1 or GameFlag_IsSet(entry.condition) != 0. The first entry passing all three tests supplies its result field; if no entry matches before the -1 terminator, the default value 18 is used. The chosen value is stored to Data_02000240[248].
evidence: The family-matcher's best guess (games/gs1/src/battle/effects/data/lookup_result.c, BattleEffect_LookupResult, score 7433/10000, below the 7500 threshold) is a real but weak structural cousin: both are '-1-terminated table of 4 s16 fields, matched against live state, GameFlag_IsSet-gated, first-match wins' scanners. But its second field is a plain -1-sentinel equality test (no bit-packed wildcard/selector), it has no alt_source-style dual id source, its GameFlag_IsSet polarity is inverted (== 0 accepts, this owner's != 0 accepts), and it is parameterized/returns a value rather than reading/writing Data_02000240 directly. Treated as a weak hint only, per task instructions; not used as a template.

A much stronger real sibling exists in-repo, already adopted exact C: games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/runtime/runtime_owner_57.c (Func_0808b1d8, main:0808b1d8) sits 328 bytes after this owner and implements the literal simpler ancestor of this exact idiom: 'while (entry[0] != -1) { if (entry[0]==first && (entry[1]==-1 || entry[1]==second)) { write two result fields; return; } entry+=4; }' reading first=Data_02000240[224], second=Data_02000240[225] -- the same two state cells this owner reads first, from a different -1-terminated table 2024 bytes further into the same ROM data region (0x0809e1d8 vs this owner's 0x0809d9f0). This confirms Data_02000240[224]/[225] as the shared 'progress id' / 'sub-state' key pair used by this whole condition-table family, and confirms the 'linear scan, first match wins, id==-1 terminator' shape independent of the weak battle-effects template.

games/gs1/asm/0808b158.s (main:0808b158, not yet adopted, 128 bytes after this owner's end) is the parameterized twin of this exact owner: same push-shuffle prologue, same ldrb-byte-3-then-0x80-mask id-source selector, same ldrh-then-mask-0x7fff-then-lsls/asrs-#17 15-bit signed wildcard-or-compare, same -1 terminator and r8 sentinel -- but arg0/arg1 replace Data_02000240[224]/[225] as inputs, the alt id source comes from calling Func_0808a8d0(arg0,arg1) (games/gs1/source-paths.json: main:0808a8d0 = battle/effects/data/get_resource_group.c) instead of reading Data_02000240[230], the table entry's second half is one 32-bit pointer field (not two s16 condition/result fields, and no GameFlag_IsSet gate), and it returns that pointer (or 0) in r0 instead of storing to Data_02000240[248]. This independently confirms every bit-level access pattern this draft uses (byte-3 flag test, halfword mask-then-signed-15-bit-compare) is this compiler's genuine idiom for this entry-flags encoding, not a bespoke reconstruction guess.

Data_02000240[224] and [225] are independently established across dozens of already-adopted owners (e.g. games/gs1/src/overlays/scene_state_interaction/run_state_interaction.c, .../scene_data/select_scene_data_by_state.c, .../ui/timed_notice/create.c) as 'signed scene/progress id' and 'signed scene sub-state', per games/gs1/src/unidentified/overlays/leaf/leaf_0092.c's comment. Data_02000240[230] and [248] have no other reader/writer anywhere in games/gs1/src, so this owner is their only known accessor; named 'alt' and the [248] destination left undescribed beyond 'scene-interaction result cell' since no independent corroboration exists for their specific role.

Func_080770c0 is independently established as GameFlag_IsSet (games/gs1/include/types.h: '#define GameFlag_IsSet Func_080770c0', also named in games/gs1/recon/en/main/080a524c.json's evidence note). games/gs1/src/game_flags/is_condition_active.c's GameFlag_IsConditionActive(condition) implements the same 'condition==-1 accepts unconditionally, otherwise accept iff GameFlag_IsSet(condition)!=0' logic this owner inlines for its entry.condition field, confirming the polarity (opposite of lookup_result.c's inverted '==0 accepts').

objdiff structural comparison (tools/compiler workbench) put this draft at 81.7% instruction match vs the raw m2c-generated hypothesis's 50.1%; m2c's own goto-soup decompilation independently reproduces the identical 'lsls #17 / asrs #17' 15-bit sign-extension and the byte-3-then-0x80 selector test this draft's bitfields already produce byte-for-byte, corroborating the struct-layout hypothesis from a second, independent tool path.
credible_shapes_tried: Current draft: `while`-rewritten as a `for (; entry->id != -1; entry++)` with `continue` for rejection (matches the reference's single shared 'entry+=8; reload id; retest' tail exactly -- an earlier `while`-loop draft with `entry++; continue;` repeated in each reject branch scored 72/82 instead of 71/78, one extra 'adds r5,#8' left un-shared).

A `do { } while` with an explicit upfront `if (entry->id != -1)` guard (spelling the compiler's own loop rotation out by hand): worse, 78 differing halfwords / 94 wrong instructions -- the compiler's own rotation of the plain `while` is more efficient than a hand-written equivalent.

Inlining Data_02000240[224]/[225]/[230] at each use site instead of hoisting them to named locals before the loop: much worse (188 candidate bytes vs 200 reference, 99 differing halfwords) -- this GCC 2.96 route does not treat the repeated per-iteration loads as loop-invariant and re-fetches them every pass, so the hoisted-local shape is confirmed necessary.

Replacing the `value:15`/`alt_source:1` bitfield pair with a plain byte-plus-halfword struct and manual `(s32)(x << 17) >> 17` shift expression instead of a signed bitfield read: worse and bigger (208 vs 200 bytes, 97 differing halfwords) -- it loses the reference's cheap 'mask with 0x7fff and compare to 0x7fff' early-exit before the sign-extend is ever computed, which the bitfield read reproduces for free. The bitfield struct is kept.

Multiple permutations of the five top-level declaration statements' textual order (progress/sub/alt/entry/result in various orders, `result=18` first, `alt` first): differing_halfwords stayed at 71-73 across every ordering tried and, critically, the *physical register* each of progress/sub/alt/result lands in did not change at all between the two 71-scoring orderings -- register color for these four cross-loop-iteration values appears to be a function of something other than C statement order for this RTL shape.
compiler_backend_evidence: Not yet investigated. The remaining 71 differing halfwords are not a differing algorithm: matched_prefix=7, candidate_bytes==owner_bytes==200 exactly, and every comparison/branch/mask/shift instruction the algorithm needs is present in both candidate and reference in the same relative order -- the diff is entirely (a) a stable 4-way register permutation (reference uses fp=progress, r7=sub, r9=alt, sl=result; this draft's compile consistently produces fp=result, r7=alt, r9=progress, sl=sub, regardless of source declaration order tried) which recolors many otherwise-identical compare/store instructions' encoded operand bits; (b) the reference rematerializes the Data_02000240 base pointer into r4 (used, then reloaded from the literal pool twice more, never saved/restored across the loop) where this draft's compile places the same rematerialized pointer in r2 -- consistent with r4 being an extra caller-saved scratch register in this ABI (the prologue never pushes/pops r4, only r5-r9/sl/fp), so both choices are equally valid to the ABI and the difference is a pure allocator preference; and (c) the reference reuses the already-computed 'base + 225*2' address plus a +10 immediate to reach 'base + 230*2', while this draft recomputes 230*2 from scratch (3 extra instructions, still netting to the same 200-byte total because of a countervailing simplification elsewhere). None of (a)-(c) is a source-shape defect as far as could be determined by inspection; they look like genuine GCC 2.96 register-allocator/rematerialization choices sensitive to RTL structure this session could not isolate by varying C statement order, loop form, or bitfield-vs-shift spelling.
remaining: 71/100 differing halfwords, 78/93 wrong instructions, at the exact 200-byte reference length. The algorithm, control flow, entry struct layout (including the id-source selector bit and the 15-bit signed wildcard field), and every callee are confirmed correct; what remains is a stable register-color permutation (fp/r7/r9/sl assigned to {progress,sub,alt,result} in a different but internally consistent order than the reference) plus one address-rematerialization register choice (r2 vs r4) and one non-reused offset computation (230*2 computed fresh instead of reusing 225*2+10). No PERM_GENERAL-searchable expression alternative or statement reordering tried moved the register permutation; per HARD CONSTRAINTS this was not forced by hand (no asm(), no register hints, no PERM_GENERAL abuse to fake a match). This is left as an honest measured draft rather than adopted.
